Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

congratulations! interjection

also congrats, I congratulate you, well done on

classical

Cic. Fam. 6.12.1: grātulor tibi, mī Balbe, vērēque grātulor
Cic. Fam. 3.12.1: ego vērō vehementer grātulor dē jūdiciō ambitūs

Grātulor (tibi)!

grātulor, grātulārī, grātulātus sum: with the dative of the person, and <span lang="la">dē</span> with the ablative, an accusative, or <span lang="la">quod</span> for the cause

Cicero’s word; grātor is poetic and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short). Traupman’s grātulātiōnēs! (p. 295) is the English plural turned into Latin.

Other words

  • Macte (virtūte estō)! — well done! good for you!

    also used · classical · Verg. A. 9.641: macte novā virtūte, puer; Traupman 295

    (Cic. (Att. 12.6.2), Liv., Verg., Hor.)

    Lewis & Short (s.v. mactus): applause or congratulation, “good luck! well done!”. See well done.

  • Dī bene vortant! — bless it! (on news of a birth, a match, a plan)

    also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 728

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    The wish that answers good news; see good luck!.

Examples

  • grātulor tibi, mī Balbe, vērēque grātulor

    congratulations, my dear Balbus, and I mean itCic. Fam. 6.12.1

  • ego vērō vehementer grātulor dē jūdiciō ambitūs

    I warmly congratulate you on the bribery verdictCic. Fam. 3.12.1

  • macte novā virtūte, puer, sīc ītur ad astra

    well done, boy, on your new courage: that’s the way to the starsVerg. A. 9.641

  • Puer nātus est. — Dī bene vortant!

    A boy’s been born. — Heaven bless him!Ter. Ad. 728

See also well done, good luck!, I’m glad for you, happy birthday!.
